claims.description: Nod3 is an intermediate regressive cell: neither the clean FD2 nor FD3

claims.tolerance: Nod3 fails the FD3 gate (no lateral+gap+heterolateral) AND the clean-FD2 gate (homolateral+frontal); its contra% and RF offset sit between LPT21 and LPT42_Nod4
claims.notes: Nod3 is regressive and cholinergic like the FD cells but its ~45% contralateral output and slightly-lateral RF place it between FD2 (LPT21) and FD3 (LPT42_Nod4); it is not assigned a single Egelhaaf identity here.

claims.description: OVERALL: FD3, FD2, and the status of Nod3 among the regressive noduli cells
claims.tolerance: LPT42 all 5 FD3 discriminators; LPT21 homolateral+frontal; Nod3 residual -> CONFIRMED
claims.notes: FD3 discriminators: LPT42_Nod4 5/5 {'D1_heterolateral': True, 'D2_rf_lateral_gap': True, 'D3_axon_crosses': True, 'D4_contra_pof': True, 'D5_family_fd3': True}. FD2: LPT21 homolateral=True frontal=True (contra 1.48%). Nod3 contra 44.66% = intermediate. Overturning condition: Nod3 would take FD3 only if it hit the four FD3 anatomy/laterality discriminators while LPT42_Nod4 failed >=2 of 5.

claims.notes: FD3 progressive-dominant (prog 0.928/reg 0.072); FD1=Nod1 regressive-dominant (prog 0.083/reg 0.917). Opposite-dominant crossed inhibition matches Egelhaaf's FD3-vs-FD1 contrast in direction; FD3's minority (regressive) channel is a trace (0.072 of classified). Annotation is power-limited (n_classified=6 of 108 contra-GABA), so the fine bidirectional/unidirectional split is not resolved by wiring alone.

claims.description: Statistical power: only one bilateral LPT42_Nod4 pair (n=2)
claims.notes: n=2 is irreducible (one bilateral pair exists). Four independent variance controls bound the inference: (i) bilateral independent replication (K.bilateral_replication); (ii) within-cell synapse bootstrap CI on the RF offset (N_BOOT=2000); (iii) in-degree permutation null for small-field selectivity (z<<0, p<=0.002); (iv) cross-version replication on v630. The conclusion does not rest on a per-cell sample size.
